summary:
I've been on a debugging kick lately with the home agent stack (Hermes-Agent), and the pattern that keeps repeating is: what looks like the model being dumb is actually an error message that dead-ends instead of naming the next step. Three separate times this week the "agent" got blamed for looping or fabricating data, and each time the real bug was in the tool wrapper. One memory tool returned "Unknown action None" on a perfectly schema-valid call because the required field only applied to a batch shape; the fix was inferring intent from the argument shape instead of failing closed. Another wrapper swallowed the upstream API's actual error text and handed the model a bare stack trace — a model can act on "seriesId is required," it can't act on a traceback, so now every wrapper passes the real message through.

The more interesting one involved a media-library tool where a grab request kept failing with an ambiguous 404 that meant two opposite things: "the ID you have is stale" or "you invented this ID." Without knowing which, the model couldn't recover, so it started guessing IDs outright. I added lightweight provenance tracking — the service remembers which IDs actually came out of a real search — so the error can now say definitively which case it is and what to do next.

Also spent time on an internal switchboard service that arbitrates GPU access across several local model backends, since they all compete for one card. Wired up a keep-warm mechanism using KV cache slot save/restore so a model that gets evicted for another workload doesn't need to reprocess the whole prompt from scratch on its next turn — that had been costing minutes on a cold reload.

Rounding it out, I patched a naming migration that broke silently after a tool-calling library upgraded its naming convention (single vs. double underscores) — old references scattered across configs and even the agent's own long-term memory kept resolving to nothing, and the failure mode read exactly like "not a valid tool" instead of "no tool by that name," which sent things down the same fabrication path as above. Consistent theme this cycle: better error messages fix more bugs than better prompts do.

highlights.oneLiner: Fixing wrapper error messages that dead-end instead of naming the next step
KV cache slot save/restore keep-warm to kill cold-reload latency
